findings.title: Validation has a side effect: should_block? writes to the DB on every validation
findings.body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` increments match_count and saves the record each time it is called. The validator calls it inside `validate_each`, which runs on every `valid?` or `save`. In `UsersController#create`, `user.valid?` runs and then `user.save` runs again, so a single signup attempt counts twice. Any later save with a changed email also bumps the counter. The validator also writes to the database inside a validation, which should be read-only. Move the stat update out of validation, or only record a match when the block actually happens.

findings.title: Non-atomic read-modify-write on match_count
findings.body: `record.match_count += 1; record.save` loads the value into Ruby, increments it, and writes it back. Concurrent signups with the same blocked email will lose updates. Use `update_all` or `increment_counter` with an atomic SQL increment instead.

findings.title: Case-sensitive exact email lookup
findings.body: `where(email: email)` is an exact, case-sensitive match. The unique index and uniqueness validation are case-sensitive as well. A blocked address `Bad@Spam.com` is bypassed by `bad@spam.com`. The rest of the app normalizes emails with `Email.downcase`. The email should be normalized when stored and when compared.

findings.title: Blocked-email check skipped when domain check fails, and nil value risks
findings.body: The block check only runs when `record.errors[attribute]` is blank. That is a deliberate guard, but it also depends on earlier validators: the presence and uniqueness errors on the same attribute suppress the blocked check and its stats. Separately, `value` can be nil. `email_in_restriction_setting?` would then compute `nil =~ regexp`, which returns nil, so a whitelist would add an error to a nil value. This is harmless when presence already fails, but the code is fragile.

findings.title: Missing newline at end of file
findings.body: The file has no trailing newline, as the diff itself shows with `\ No newline at end of file`.

findings.title: rejectedEmails array is shared across all controller instances
findings.body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` is defined on the class prototype, so one array instance is shared by every instance and persists. `pushObject` mutates that shared array. Initialize it in `init` instead. The property dependency `'rejectedEmails.@each'` is also non-standard; it should be `rejectedEmails.[]`.

findings.title: Failed-create response exposes values and error details to client, enabling blocklist probing
findings.body: The failure response now returns `user.errors.to_hash` and the submitted values. Combined with the `blocked` error message and the client rejecting only that email, this lets anyone probe whether specific addresses are on the block list. The client rejects any email error, including 'has already been taken', not just blocked ones. `user.attributes.slice` is also an unnecessarily broad way to echo input; `params` would do.

findings.title: No test of the validator integration with User
findings.body: The specs stub `should_block?` for the validator and never test that a `User` with a blocked email is invalid. They also don't cover interaction with the whitelist/blacklist domain settings. The refactor moved the domain validation from `User` into a new validator, so the domain restriction behavior now has no test coverage in the new spec files.
